# Homer, *Iliad* — conventions (pilot, 2026-10-12)

The Iliad is read exactly as the Odyssey is. **Everything in `../odyssey/conventions.md` applies here** —
language-level choices (reconstructed Attic after Allen, *Vox Graeca*; the `tr` scheme; U+2019 elision;
U+00B7 ano teleia; `langCode: null`; `script: "greek"`; `trStyle: "line"`), verse and segmentation,
the two English layers, the Homeric-Greek flags, the sole-source rule and lexical aids, the glossary-entry
format, notes, scansion — and **its house-renderings table is binding for the Iliad too**: a formula or
epithet the Odyssey has fixed keeps its English here. The scanner (`scan_hexameter.py`) and the
transliterator (`translit_grc.py`) are the Odyssey's own, imported, not copied. Below is only what the
Iliad changes or adds.

## Edition of record

**D. B. Monro and T. W. Allen, *Homeri Opera*, tomi I–II (Iliad), 3rd ed. (Oxford Classical Texts;
Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1920)** — Greek text only. Pre-1930, public domain everywhere. Machine-readable
copy: Perseus TEI `PerseusDL/canonical-greekLit`, `tlg0012.tlg001.perseus-grc2.xml` (TEI sha256
`ae8b617018c6e5af14cbab9ce6082438c0f103eafd0a4c67bdae4588cca5eaa4`), archived by `archive_iliad.py` into `source/iliad-monro-allen1920.json`.
There is no public-domain English printed with it; for a meaning-check on a hard passage, the old
public-domain translations (e.g. Murray's Loeb Iliad, 1924) may be consulted silently under the KJV rule,
never for wording, never shipped.

Text kept exactly as the archive prints it, with the Odyssey's two mechanical normalisations (U+02BC →
U+2019 for elision, NFC). The OCT prints the diaeresis (`ἐϋκνήμιδες`, `ἠΰκομος`, `ὀϊστοί`) and
prints `ἤτοι` as one word and `τοὶ γάρ` as two; keep all of these as printed. No quotation marks round
speeches, as in Murray.

Known features of this archive (from `archive_iliad.py`):
- 9.458–461 are not in the text (the edition gives them only in the apparatus); numbering jumps 457 → 462.
- Numbering also jumps at 11.542 → 544 and 14.268 → 270.
- 8.548 and 8.550–552 are printed in square brackets (athetized); the archive keeps them inside `[ ]`.
  The reader's word regex ignores the brackets. The note on the unit says what the brackets mean.

## Sectioning

The 24 books are the authentic division and the manifest `group` ("Book 1"). Inside a book the parts are
cut **only at paragraph breaks the edition prints** (1,055 in the poem), aiming at ~100 lines: 159 parts
(median 98 lines). Three parts fall outside the 55–135 band because the edition's paragraphs leave no
better cut: 9.430–605 (172 lines, Phoenix's speech), 11.655–803 (149, Nestor's tale) and 11.804–848 (45).
Part ids `iliad-NNN`, `seq` on every manifest entry; `part` = our English name + citation,
`The Wrath and the Plague (1.1–100)`.

## The three names of the army — a departure from the Odyssey

The Odyssey's `i` layer renders Δαναοί as "Greeks". **The Iliad does not**: Ἀχαιοί "Achaeans",
Δαναοί "Danaans", Ἀργεῖοι "Argives" in both layers, always, because the Iliad alternates the three
constantly and the reader should hear which one the poet chose. "Greeks" is used in neither layer.

## Sharing English with the Odyssey

`packet.py` lists every line of a part that already stands in a published Odyssey unit, with its English,
and `validate_iliad.py` warns (does not fail) when an Iliad unit has the same Greek as an Odyssey unit
but different English. Reuse the Odyssey's English unless the Iliad context forbids it; a departure is
recorded in the part's `new-renderings.md` with the reason. Inside the Iliad, the Odyssey's hard rule
holds: the same Greek gets the same English (enforced by the validator).

## House renderings — Iliad additions (fixed at the pilot, 2026-10-12)

The opening is our own. "Wrath" for μῆνις is the old, pre-modern rendering, chosen because the word is
specifically a lasting, god-sized anger (Calchas uses it of Apollo at 1.75), and because "rage" and
"anger" are the distinctive choices of the best-known modern versions.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| μῆνιν ἄειδε θεὰ Πηληϊάδεω Ἀχιλῆος (1.1, house rendering of the opening) | "The wrath sing, goddess, of Peleus’-son Achilles" | "Goddess, sing the wrath of Peleus’ son Achilles" | "rage", "anger" (the famous modern choices), "Sing, goddess, the anger of…", "Rage — Goddess, sing the rage…", "Sing of the cataclysmic wrath"; "wrath" is the old, pre-modern rendering and the word μῆνις needs: a lasting, god-sized anger |
| μῆνις | "wrath" | "wrath" | "rage", "anger" (kept for χόλος), "fury"; χόλος stays "anger", κότος "resentment" (as in the Odyssey table) |
| οὐλομένην (of the wrath, 1.2) | "the ruinous one" | "the ruinous wrath" | "accursed", "murderous", "destructive", "cataclysmic"; keeps the Odyssey's οὐλόμενος "ruinous" |
| μυρί’ … ἄλγε’ ἔθηκε (1.2) | "countless pains laid" | "laid countless pains on" | "thousandfold", "immeasurable pain", "countless losses", "incalculable pain" |

| ἑκηβόλος (Ἀπόλλων) | "far-shooting" | "far-shooting" (+ note: usual explanation) | "far-darting" (kept for ἑκατηβελέτης), "the archer", "who strikes from afar" |

| τὸν δ’ ἠμείβετ’ ἔπειτα βοῶπις πότνια Ἥρη (1.551, whole-line reply-formula) | "Him then answered ox-eyed lady Hera:" | "Then ox-eyed lady Hera answered him:" | "white-armed" (λευκώλενος, a different epithet, 1.595), "queen Hera" |

| αἰθαλόεν (2.415) | "soot-blackened" | "soot-blackened" | "smoky", "sooty" (the Odyssey table’s `l` for αἰθαλόεις 22.239 is "sooty"; the compound reads better with the roof, and `i` there is also "soot-blackened"); extends the Odyssey table’s αἰθαλόεις |
| πυρὸς δηΐοιο (2.415) | "hostile fire" | "hostile fire" | "enemy fire", "devouring fire", "raging fire", "consuming fire"; δήϊος "hostile" |
| θύρετρα (2.415) | "doors" | "doors" | "gates", "doorways"; keeps the Odyssey’s "doors" (22.137) |

| ὀδὰξ λαζοίατο γαῖαν (2.418) | "may take the earth with their teeth" | "bite the earth" | "lick the dust", "seize the ground", "kiss the earth" (each changes the gesture); ὀδάξ "with the teeth" |
| ἑταῖροι (2.417) | "companions" | "companions" | "comrades", "friends", "men"; keeps the Odyssey’s "companions" |
| ὣς ἔφατ’, οὐδ’ ἄρα πώ οἱ ἐπεκραίαινε Κρονίων (2.419) | "So he spoke, but not yet for him did the son of Cronus bring it to fulfilment" | "So he spoke, but the son of Cronus did not yet fulfil it for him" | "grant" (reserved for δίδωμι with a thing given), "answer"; ἐπικραιαίνω "bring to fulfilment" |
| ἀμέγαρτον πόνον (2.420) | "the unenviable toil" | "the dreadful toil" | "unwished-for", "grievous", "pitiless"; follows the Odyssey’s ἀμέγαρτον ἀυτμήν "unenviable" / "dreadful" |

| πάντες ἐϋπλεκέες (2.449) | "all well-plaited" | "every one finely plaited" | "well-woven", "braided"; πλέκω "plait", ἐΰ- "well" |
| ἑκατόμβοιος (2.449) | "worth a hundred oxen" | "worth a hundred oxen" | "a hundred-oxen's value", "worth a hecatomb" (a hecatomb is a sacrifice, not a price); ἑκατόν + βοῦς |
| παιφάσσουσα διέσσυτο (2.450; παιφάσσω rare) | "darting about … rushed through" | "darted about and rushed through" | "flashing", "gleaming" (each picks one guess), "sweeping"; διασεύω "rush through" |
| λαὸν Ἀχαιῶν (2.450) | "the people of the Achaeans" | "the army of the Achaeans" | "the host", "the men"; follows the shipped 2.163 (κατὰ λαὸν Ἀχαιῶν "through the people" / "through the army") |
| ὀτρύνουσ’ ἰέναι (2.451) | "urging them to go" | "urging them forward" | "bidding", "rousing" (kept for ὄρνυμι ἐν … ὦρσεν, 2.451); ὀτρύνω keeps "urge" (the Odyssey table sets it against ἄνωχθι "bid") |
| ἐν … ὦρσεν (2.451) | "roused in" | "roused in the heart of each man" | "stirred", "put into", "kindled"; ὄρνυμι "rouse", tmesis |

| ὀρνίθων πετεηνῶν (2.459) | "winged birds" | "winged birds" | "feathered", "flying"; πετεηνός "winged", as in the Odyssey table’s ἐλαφρότατος πετεηνῶν "lightest of winged things" |

| τῷ / τοῖς / τοῖσι δ’ ἅμα (ἅμ’) + number + μέλαιναι νῆες ἕποντο (2.524, 2.534, 2.545, 2.556, 2.568, whole-line closing formula of a Catalogue entry) | "And with them (him) forty black ships followed." | "And with them (him) forty black ships followed." | "ships followed them", "black ships went with them" (loses ἅμα), "dark ships"; μέλας "black" as in the Odyssey’s νηῦς μέλαινα; ἕπομαι "follow", kept apart from κίον "went" (2.509) and ἐστιχόωντο (2.516); `l` = `i` because the line is a counted formula and the number is what changes |
| τῶν αὖθ’ ἡγεμόνευ’ + name (2.540, 2.552, 2.563, whole-line leader formula) | "Of these again was leader X" | "Of these, in turn, X was the leader" | "led them again", "was their commander" (ἀρχός is "commander"), "of these X had command"; αὖθ’ = αὖθι, a by-form of αὖθις / αὖτε, "again, in turn", ἡγεμονεύω "be leader" (the Odyssey’s "led the way" is for a guide on a road) |
| ἦρχον (+ genitive of a people, 2.494, 2.512, 2.517) | "were leading" | "led" (or "were led by", when the people are the subject, 2.511) | "ruled", "were commanders" (reserved for ἀρχός), "commanded"; ἄρχω "lead" as in iliad-010 (ἄρχευ’ "lead") |
| ἡγεμονεύω / ἡγέομαι (2.527, 2.567) | "was leader" · "was leading" | "was leader" · "led" | "marched at the head", "was in command"; ἡγεμονεύω "be leader" and ἡγέομαι "lead" are kept apart |
| κοσμέω · διακοσμέω (κοσμῆσαι 2.554, διεκόσμεον 2.476) | "to set in order" · "set in order" | "to marshal" · "set in order" (the leaders) | "arrange", "array", "deck out" (the Odyssey’s κόσμος is "order" and "contriving"); `i` "marshal" in the skill (κοσμῆσαι), "set in order" for the act |
| ἐρίζω (of skill, Νέστωρ οἶος ἔριζεν, 2.555) | "rivalled" | "rivalled" | "quarrelled" (ἐρίζω of strife is "quarrel", 2.214 and 2.247), "vied with", "competed"; the Odyssey’s ἐρίζω "rival" for skill |
| ἱλάομαι (ἱλάονται, 2.550) | "appease" | "appease" | "propitiate", "placate", "worship"; the same verb as ἱλάσκομαι "appease" (1.386) |
| ἔσπετε νῦν μοι Μοῦσαι (2.484, whole-line invocation) | "Tell now to me, Muses," | "Tell me now, Muses," | "Sing", "Speak" (ἄειδε is "sing", 1.1), "Declare"; ἐνέπω "tell" as in the Odyssey’s ἔννεπε |
| Ὀλύμπια δώματ’ ἔχουσαι (2.484, feminine) · Ὀλυμπιάδες Μοῦσαι (2.491) | "who hold the Olympian halls" · "the Olympian Muses" | "you who hold the halls of Olympus" · "the Olympian Muses" | "Muses of Olympus" (for Ὀλυμπιάδες), "who dwell on Olympus"; the table’s Ὀλύμπια δώματ’ ἔχοντες in the feminine |
| κλέος οἶον ἀκούομεν (2.486) | "we hear a report alone" | "we hear only a report" | "fame", "rumour", "glory" (κλέος ἐσθλόν is "good fame"); κλέος "report" as in the Odyssey table’s κλέος "report" (16.461) |
| οὐκ ἂν … μυθήσομαι οὐδ’ ὀνομήνω (2.488) | "I could not tell, nor could I name it" | "I could not tell, nor name" | "I could not recount", "nor mention"; follows the Odyssey’s same words at 4.240 (also 11.328, 11.517) |
| δέκα μὲν γλῶσσαι, δέκα δὲ στόματ’ … φωνὴ ἄρρηκτος, χάλκεον … ἦτορ (2.489–490) | "ten tongues, and ten mouths … a voice unbreakable, and a heart of bronze for me were within" | "ten tongues were mine, and ten mouths, and an unbreakable voice, and a heart of bronze within me" | "unbroken voice", "iron voice", "tireless", "brazen heart"; ἄρρηκτος "unbreakable" (Odyssey), χάλκεος "of bronze", ἦτορ "heart" |
| μνησαίατο (μιμνήσκομαι, 2.492) | "call to mind" | "call to mind" | "remind me of", "remember" (no object "me" in the Greek), "tell"; μιμνήσκομαι "call to mind" |
| ἀρχοὺς … νηῶν (2.493) | "the commanders of the ships" | "the commanders of the ships" | "captains", "leaders" (reserved for ἡγεμών, ἡγήτωρ); follows the Iliad’s ἀρχός "commander" (1.311) |
| προπάσας (νῆάς τε προπάσας, 2.493) | "all of them" | "all" | "every single one", "all together" (reserved for συμπάντων / πάντων ἅμα) |
| ἔθνεα πολλά (of flies, 2.469) | "the many tribes" | "the many swarms" | follows the table’s ἔθνεα "tribes" / "swarms" (2.87, 2.91, 2.459, 2.464) |
| ἁδινάων μυιάων (2.469) | "thronging" | "thronging" | "buzzing", "restless" (kept for the table’s ἁδινάων "thronging", of the bees at 2.87) |
| μεταπρέπω (βόεσσι μεταπρέπει, 2.481) | "is conspicuous among" | "is conspicuous among" | "stands out among" (the Odyssey’s `i` for μεταπρέπει, 10.525 and 11.33; here it would repeat ἔξοχος "stands out" in the unit before), "excels among" |
| ἔξοχος (μέγ’ ἔξοχος ἔπλετο, 2.480; ἔξοχον ἡρώεσσιν, 2.483) | "greatly standing out" · "standing out" | "stands out far above" · "standing out" | "outstanding", "pre-eminent" (reserved, see the table’s ἔξοχος Ἀχαιῶν), "supreme"; follows the table’s ἔξοχος "stood out" |
| ἐκπρεπής (ἐκπρεπέ’ ἐν πολλοῖσι, 2.483) | "distinguished" | "distinguished" | "conspicuous" (reserved for ἀριδείκετος and μεταπρέπω), "eminent", "outstanding" (ἀριπρεπής), "splendid" (ἀγλαός) |
| ἀγέληφι (2.480) | "in the herd" | "in a herd" | "in the herd of cattle"; -φι is the old ending that serves as a dative |
| ἄγγεα (γλάγος ἄγγεα δεύει, 2.471) | "the vessels" | "the vessels" | "the pails" (the Odyssey’s `i` for γαυλοί, 9.222–223, where ἄγγεα stays "vessels"), "the jars", "the bowls" |
| ἠλάσκω (2.470) | "roam" | "roam" | "wander", "flit", "buzz"; ἠλάσκω "wander about" |
| ὑσμίνην ἰέναι (2.477) | "to go into battle" | "to go into battle" | "to enter the fray"; ὑσμίνη "battle" as in the Odyssey and iliad-007, iliad-010 |
| ὄζος Ἄρηος (Ἐλεφήνωρ, 2.540) | "scion of Ares" | "scion of Ares" | "offshoot", "branch", "descendant", "darling of Ares"; literally "branch", used of a descendant |
| ἀσπιδιώτης (ἀνέρας ἀσπιδιώτας, 2.554) | "shield-bearing" | "shield-bearing" | "shielded", "shield-men", "armed with shields" |
| λινοθώρηξ (2.529) | "linen-breastplated" | "wore a linen breastplate" | "linen-corsleted", "linen-armoured"; θώραξ is "breastplate" at every occurrence (2.544 θώρηκας "breastplates") |
| ἐκέκαστο (ἐγχείῃ ἐκέκαστο, 2.530) | "excelled" | "excelled" | "surpassed" (reserved for νικάω, 2.370), "outdid", "was better than"; follows the Odyssey’s ἐκέκαστο "excelled" (odyssey-006 and odyssey-044) |
| Πανέλληνες (2.530) | "the Hellenes all together" | "all the Hellenes" | "all Greeks" (Greeks is avoided in both layers), "the whole of Hellas"; follows the table’s Παναχαιῶν "of the Achaeans all together" / "of all the Achaeans" |
| μείων (2.528–529, in stature) | "smaller" | "smaller" | "lesser" (the rank), "lower", "shorter"; the comparative of μικρός / ὀλίγος |
| Τελαμώνιος Αἴας | "Telamonian Ajax" | "Telamonian Ajax" | "Ajax son of Telamon", "greater Ajax"; the adjective is kept to tell the two Ajaxes apart, with ταχὺς Αἴας Ὀϊλῆος "swift Ajax, son of Oileus" |
| μένεα πνείοντες (2.536) | "breathing might" | "breathing might" | "breathing strength" (the Odyssey’s 22.203; a departure, with the reason: the Iliad has μένος "might" at 2.387 and keeps "strength" for κράτος and σθένος), "breathing fury" (reserved for μένος of anger), "breathing courage" |

| κρατέρ’ ἄλγεα πάσχων (2.721) | "suffering harsh pains" | "suffering harsh pains" | "strong pains", "severe pains" (the Odyssey ships all three in different places); follows odyssey-022, where the same half-line is said of Odysseus lying on Calypso's island |
| μοχθίζω (μοχθίζοντα, 2.723) | "toiling" | "suffering" | "labouring", "struggling", "in agony" (adds a degree); μοχθέω is "toil" and the sense here is the effect of the wound |
| ὕδρος (ὀλοόφρονος ὕδρου, 2.723) | "water-snake" | "water-snake" | "hydra" (a proper name of the monster), "serpent", "viper"; ὕδρος is ὕδωρ's snake, and ὀλοόφρων keeps the Odyssey's "baleful-minded" |
| ἔνθ’ ὅ γε κεῖτ’ ἀχέων (2.724) | "There he lay grieving" | "There he lay grieving" | "groaning", "in anguish"; follows the Odyssey (odyssey-052, "There he lies grieving"); ἀχέω "grieve" |
| νόθος (Ὀϊλῆος νόθος υἱός, 2.727) | "bastard" | "illegitimate" | "base-born", "natural son", "bastard" in `i` (loaded in modern English); the word is "born outside marriage" |
| πτολίπορθος (Ὀϊλῆϊ πτολιπόρθῳ, 2.728) | "city-sacking" | "sacker of cities" | "city-destroyer", "destroyer of cities"; follows the Odyssey's πτολιπόρθιος "city-sacking" / "sacker of cities" (odyssey-070), and πέρθω stays "sack" |
| κλωμακόεις (Ἰθώμην κλωμακόεσσαν, 2.729) | "stony" | "stony" (+ note: sense not certain, "terraced" another reading) | "rocky" (reserved for πετρήεις, 2.496), "craggy" (σκόπελος "crag"), "terraced" (decides the open sense); κλῶμαξ "heap of stones" |
| τρηχεῖαν (Ὀλιζῶνα τρηχεῖαν, 2.717) | "rough" | "rough" | "rugged" (the Odyssey's wording for a shore, odyssey-026), "harsh"; follows iliad-013's "rough Aegilips" (2.633) |
| ἰητῆρ’ ἀγαθώ (2.732, dual) | "two good healers" | "good healers both" | "doctors", "physicians", "skilled in medicine"; ἰητήρ keeps the Odyssey's "healer", and the dual is shown by "two" and "both" |
| κάρηνα (Τιτάνοιό τε λευκὰ κάρηνα, 2.735) | "peaks" | "peaks" | "heads" (kept for the Iliad's cities at 2.117 and the Odyssey's "heads" of the dead), "summits"; κάρηνα of mountains is "peaks", as in the Odyssey's ὀρέων … κάρηνα |
| λευκός (πόλιν Ὀλοοσσόνα λευκήν, 2.739; λευκὰ κάρηνα, 2.735) | "white" | "white" | "gleaming" (kept for the Odyssey's γλαυκῶπις), "bright" (kept for ἀργός), "chalky"; ἀργινόεις stays "bright-white" |
| Φῆρες · λαχνήεις (Φῆρας … λαχνήεντας, 2.743) | "the hairy beasts" | "the hairy beasts" | "Centaurs" (names what the Greek leaves unnamed, as at 1.268), "shaggy" (reserved for λάσιος, 1.189), "wild"; φήρ is "beast" and λαχνήεις "hairy" |
| ἐτίσατο (Φῆρας ἐτίσατο, 2.743) | "took vengeance on" | "took vengeance on" | "avenged himself on", "punished", "repaid"; the middle of τίνω, with the person as object; τίσασθαι "to avenge" (2.590) has a thing as object, and `l`/`i` there are the same verb |
| ὦσε … πέλασσεν (2.744) | "thrust … brought near" | "pushed … forced on to" | "drove" (reserved for ἐλαύνω and στυφελίζω), "banished"; ὠθέω "push", πελάζω "bring near" |
| οὐκ οἶος (2.745) | "not alone" | "did not lead alone" (the verb supplied from 740, as the note says) | "not by himself"; οἶος "alone" |
| δυσχείμερος (Δωδώνην δυσχείμερον, 2.750) | "harsh-wintered" | "of the harsh winters" | "wintry" (reserved for χειμέριος, the Odyssey's "wintry" storms), "stormy", "cold"; δυσ- "ill" + χεῖμα "winter" |
| οἰκί’ ἔθεντο (2.750) | "made their homes" | "made their homes" | "set up houses", "built their dwellings" (decides how); οἰκία "homes", τίθεμαι "make, set up" |
| ἔργα νέμοντο (Τιταρησσόν, 2.751) | "inhabited the farmlands" | "inhabited the farmlands" | "tilled the fields" (νέμομαι is "inhabit"), "had their farmlands" (that is ἔχω "hold", kept apart from νέμομαι through the Catalogue), "held the works"; ἔργα as the tilled land, and νέμομαι keeps "inhabit" |
| ἱμερτός (Τιταρησσόν, 2.751) | "lovely" | "lovely" | "desirable", "charming"; the Odyssey ships "lovely" for ἱμερτός / ἱμερόεις |
| καλλίρροος (ὕδωρ, 2.752) | "fair-flowing" | "fair-flowing" | "beautifully-flowing"; καλλι- "fair" + ῥόος "stream"; chosen here, no published Odyssey unit has the word |
| ἀργυροδίνης (Πηνειῷ ἀργυροδίνῃ, 2.753) | "silver-eddying" | "silver-eddying" | "silver-swirling", "silvery", "with silver whirlpools"; ἀργυρο- "silver" + δίνη "eddy", the stock epithet of a river |
| ἠΰτ’ ἔλαιον (2.754) | "like olive-oil" | "like olive oil" | "like oil" alone (loses the plant); ἠΰτε "like" (1.359) |
| ὅρκου δεινοῦ Στυγὸς ὕδατος … ἀπορρώξ (2.755) | "of the dread oath, the water of the Styx … an offshoot" | "an offshoot of the water of the Styx, the dread oath" | "branch", "tributary", "outlet" (the Odyssey ships "offshoot" for ἀπορρώξ of Cocytus, 10.514, and "the water of the Styx" for the same half-line Στυγὸς ὕδατός ἐστιν ἀπορρώξ); the three genitives are kept in apposition |
| ναίεσκον (2.758) | "kept dwelling" | "dwelt" | "used to dwell", "would dwell" (the iterative suffix is shown by "kept" in `l`); ναίω "dwell" kept apart from νέμομαι and ἔχω through the Catalogue |
| θοός (Πρόθοος θοός, 2.758) | "swift" | "swift" | "quick", "nimble", "fleet" (reserved for ποδώκης); θοός "swift", as of ships in the Odyssey |
| κοίρανοι (2.760) | "rulers" | "rulers" | "lords" (reserved for ἄναξ), "princes", "captains"; keeps the Odyssey's κοίρανος "ruler" |
| ὄχ’ ἄριστος (τίς τὰρ τῶν ὄχ’ ἄριστος ἔην, 2.761) | "by far the best" | "far the best" | "the very best", "the finest of them"; follows οἰωνοπόλων ὄχ’ ἄριστος (1.69) |
| ἔννεπε Μοῦσα (σύ μοι ἔννεπε Μοῦσα, 2.761) | "do you tell me, Muse" | "tell me, Muse" | "sing" (reserved for ἀείδω), "declare"; keeps the Odyssey's ἔννεπε "tell" and iliad-012's ἔσπετε "tell" |
| μέγ’ ἄρισται (ἵπποι, 2.763) | "by far the best" | "by far the best" | "the best of all", "far the finest"; μέγα as an adverb, "by far", while ὄχα is "far" |
| Φηρητιάδαο (2.763) | "Pheres’-son" | "the son of Pheres" (+ note: the man meant is usually taken to be Admetus) | "Pheres’ son" (the patronymic is hyphenated in `l` as at Ἀτρεΐδης "Atreus’-son"), "Pheretiades", "descendant of Pheres" (a patronymic does not always mean the son); the name is not given in the Greek |
| ὄτριχας οἰέτεας (2.765) | "alike in hair, of one age" | "alike in hair, of one age" (+ note: sense not certain) | "of one coat", "of equal years", "matched in colour"; ὄτριχας is perhaps ὁμο- + θρίξ, οἰέτεας probably οἶος "one" + ἔτος "year", and neither is certain |
| σταφύλῃ ἐπὶ νῶτον ἐΐσας (2.765) | "well-balanced along the back by the plumb-line" | "well-balanced along the back as if by the plumb-line" | "level", "even" (reserved against ἐΐσας "well-balanced"), "straight as a plumb-line"; ἐΐσας keeps the "well-balanced" of νῆας ἐΐσας (1.306), and σταφύλη is a plumb-line |
| ποδώκης (ποδώκεας, 2.764) | "fleet-footed" | "fleet-footed" | "swift-footed" (reserved for ποδάρκης), "swift of foot" (πόδας ὠκύς); πούς + ὠκύς |
| θρέψ’ (τρέφω, 2.766) | "reared" | "reared" | "nursed", "fed", "bred"; keeps the "reared" of Athena and Erechtheus (θρέψε, 2.548) |
| θηλείας (ἵππους, 2.767) | "female" | "mares" | "female horses", "she-horses"; ἵπποι is feminine here and the note says the pair are mares |
| φόβον Ἄρηος φορεούσας (2.767) | "carrying the terror of Ares" | "carrying the terror of battle" | "bearing the panic of Ares", "carrying flight", "fear of the war-god"; Ἄρηος as war (2.401, μῶλον Ἄρηος), φόβος "terror" |
| μήνιεν (ὄφρ’ Ἀχιλεὺς μήνιεν, 2.769) | "was wrathful" | "was wrathful" | "was angry", "nursed his wrath", "raged"; keeps ἐμήνιε "was wrathful" (1.247) |
| ἀπομηνίσας (κεῖτ’ ἀπομηνίσας, 2.772) | "withdrawn in wrath" | "withdrawn in wrath" (+ note: the force of ἀπο- is not certain) | "ceased from wrath", "having raged out his anger", "in full wrath" (each decides ἀπο-); μηνίω "be wrathful" + ἀπο- "away", with the dative of the one he is wrathful at |
| κορωνίς · ποντοπόρος (νήεσσι κορωνίσι ποντοπόροισι, 2.771) | "curved, sea-crossing" | "curved, sea-crossing" | "beaked", "sea-faring", "sea-going", "hollow" (reserved for γλαφυρός / κοῖλος); Odyssey table, unchanged |
| φέρτατος (πολὺ φέρτατος, 2.769) | "by far the best" | "by far the best" | "the strongest" (κάρτιστοι), "mightiest"; keeps the Odyssey's πολὺ φέρτατος "by far the best" |
| φορέεσκον (2.770) | "kept carrying" | "carried" | "used to carry", "were wont to carry"; φορέω "carry", the iterative shown by "kept" in `l` |
| τέρποντο … ἱέντες (δίσκοισιν … αἰγανέῃσιν … τόξοισιν, 2.774–775) | "were taking delight … throwing" | "were amusing themselves throwing the discus and the javelin, and shooting with bows" | "enjoyed", "took pleasure"; the line is the Odyssey's (4.626), reused for its own words, with ἱέντες "throwing" governing the bows of the next half-line as "shooting" |
| ῥηγμίν (παρὰ ῥηγμῖνι θαλάσσης, 2.773) | "the surf-line of the sea" | "the shore where the sea breaks" | "the beach", "the water's edge"; follows iliad-005 and the Odyssey |
| λωτός (2.776) | "lotus" | "lotus" (+ note: here a fodder plant) | "clover" (decides the plant; the Odyssey does ship "clover" for the λωτός of the plain of Sparta, 4.603, a pasture list, but the half-line λωτὸν ἐρεπτόμενοι is "feeding on lotus" there, 9.97, and the Iliad keeps the half-line), "water-lily", "trefoil"; the Odyssey ships "lotus" for λωτός of the Lotus-eaters and says which plant is not known |
| ἐλεόθρεπτος (σέλινον, 2.776) | "marsh-nurtured" | "marsh-nurtured" | "marsh-fed", "marsh-bred", "growing in the marsh" (drops θρέπτος); ἕλος "marsh" + τρέφω "nurture", as in the table's διοτρεφής "Zeus-nurtured" |
| σέλινον (2.776) | "celery" | "celery" (+ note: celery or a like plant) | "parsley", "wild celery", "marsh-parsley"; the plant is not told apart from its near relatives |
| ἐρέπτομαι (ἐρεπτόμενοι, 2.776) | "feeding on" | "feeding on" | "eating", "grazing", "browsing", "cropping"; keeps the Odyssey's λωτὸν ἐρεπτόμενοι "feeding on lotus" (odyssey-039; πυρὸν ἐρεπτομένους "eating wheat", odyssey-097, has another object) |
| ἕστασαν (2.777) | "stood" | "stood" | "had stood", "were standing" (it is the pluperfect of ἵστημι with a past sense) |
| πεπυκασμένα (ἅρματα δ’ εὖ πεπυκασμένα, 2.777) | "well covered" | "well covered" | "well wrapped", "closely covered", "well built" (the other sense of πυκάζω); πυκάζω "cover closely", kept apart from πυκινός "shrewd" |
| ἀρηΐφιλος (ἀρχὸν ἀρηΐφιλον, 2.778) | "Ares-loved" | "dear to Ares" | "war-loving", "beloved of Ares"; follows the Odyssey's ἀρηΐφιλος Μενέλαος "Ares-loved Menelaus" / "Menelaus, dear to Ares" (15.169) |
| φοιτάω (φοίτων, 2.779) | "went to and fro" | "went to and fro" | "roamed", "wandered", "kept coming and going"; keeps the Odyssey's "went to and fro" (odyssey-069) |
| οὐδὲ μάχοντο (2.779) | "and did not fight" | "and did not fight" | "nor fought" in `i`, "held back from battle"; μάχομαι "fight" |
| νέμοιτο (πυρὶ χθὼν πᾶσα νέμοιτο, 2.780, of fire) | "were being fed upon" | "were being consumed" | "grazed", "ranged over", "devoured" (kept for the fire of ἀΐδηλον, 2.455); νέμομαι is "inhabit" of men in the Catalogue (2.751, 2.835), and the note says it is a different sense here |
| ὑπεστενάχιζε (2.781) | "groaned beneath" | "groaned beneath" | "groaned under", "rumbled", "shuddered"; στεναχίζω keeps "groan" (1.364), with ὑπο- shown |
| Ἀρίμοις (εἰν Ἀρίμοις, 2.783) | "among the Arimi" | "among the Arimi" | "in Arima" (decides a place), "among the Arimians"; people or place not known, and the note says so |
| εὐνάς (Τυφωέος ἔμμεναι εὐνάς, 2.783) | "the beds of Typhoeus" | "Typhoeus has his bed" | "lair", "resting place" (each decides the sense), "couches"; the plural is one lair |
| διαπρήσσω + genitive (διέπρησσον πεδίοιο, 2.785) | "were crossing" | "were crossing" | "accomplishing" (the table keeps that for διαπρήσσουσα κέλευθον, which has its object), "making their way through"; the genitive is the ground covered |
| ποδήνεμος Ἶρις (2.786) | "wind-footed" | "wind-footed" | "wind-swift" (ἄνεμος + πούς, not ἀελλόπος), "storm-footed", "swift as the wind" (adds a comparison), "fleet-footed" (reserved for ποδώκης); ὠκέα Ἶρις alone is "swift Iris" |
| πόδας ὠκέα Ἶρις (2.790, 2.795) | "swift-in-feet Iris" | "Iris, swift of foot" | "swift-footed" (ποδάρκης), "fleet-footed" (ποδώκης); the feminine of the table’s πόδας ὠκὺς Ἀχιλλεύς |
| ἀγχοῦ δ’ ἱσταμένη προσέφη πόδας ὠκέα Ἶρις (2.790; departure from the Odyssey’s ἀγχοῦ δ’ ἱσταμένη προσέφη γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη, odyssey-071 and iliad-008) | "And standing close by, swift-in-feet Iris spoke;" | "Iris, swift of foot, came and stood close by, and spoke;" | "addressed him" / "said to him" (the shipped Odyssey and iliad-008 wording; in them a person is addressed at once, while here the Greek names no one until 795 and the speech starts only at 796), "addressed them" (supplies the assembly) |
| ἀγγελίη ἀλεγεινή (σὺν ἀγγελίῃ ἀλεγεινῇ, 2.787) | "grievous news" | "grievous news" | "message" (the Odyssey’s draft word, withdrawn), "tidings", "painful report"; follows the Odyssey’s ἀγγελίη "news" and ἀλεγεινός "grievous" |
| ἀγορὰς ἀγόρευον (2.788) | "were holding assemblies" | "were meeting in assembly" | "were declaring assemblies", "were making speeches" (the cognate noun is kept visible in `l`); ἀγορεύω is "declare" in a public pronouncement, and with its own noun it is "hold assembly" |
| ὁμηγερής (ὁμηγερέες, 2.789) | "gathered together" | "gathered together" | "assembled", "met together"; ὁμο- "same" + ἀγείρω "gather" |
| εἴσατο φθογγήν (2.791) | "made herself like in voice" | "made herself like … in voice" | "took the voice of" (loses εἴσατο), "imitated"; the aorist middle of εἴδομαι, kept as in ἐεισάμενος "making himself like" (2.22) |
| σκοπός (Τρώων σκοπός, 2.792) | "lookout" | "lookout" | "scout", "watchman", "spy"; σκοπέω "look" |
| ποδωκείη (ποδωκείῃσι πεποιθώς, 2.792) | "fleet-footedness" | "speed of foot" | "his legs", "swiftness" alone; the abstract noun of ποδώκης "fleet-footed", and πεποιθώς is "trusting in" |
| τύμβος (τύμβῳ ἐπ’ ἀκροτάτῳ, 2.793) | "on the topmost tomb" | "on the very top of the tomb" | "mound", "barrow" (the Odyssey’s "mound" at 3.239, but iliad-013 ships "tomb" for τύμβος in the Iliad), "highest"; ἀκρότατος keeps "topmost" as in ἀκροτάτῃ κορυφῇ "on the topmost peak" |
| δέγμενος ὁππότε … ἀφορμηθεῖεν (2.794) | "waiting for when … should set out" | "waiting for the moment when … should set out" | "watching for", "ready for"; the optative marks an expected event, and δέχομαι "receive" is "wait for" |
| ὦ γέρον (2.796) | "Old man" | "Old man" | "Father", "Sire", "Elder"; "old man" is reserved for ὦ γέρον in the Odyssey table (cf. πάτερ ὦ ξεῖνε) |
| μῦθοι φίλοι ἄκριτοί (2.796) | "words … dear, unsorted" | "endless talk … dear" | "indecisive", "confused" (the Odyssey’s "indistinct" for ἀκριτόμυθοι, a different word), "undecided"; ἄκριτος keeps the Iliad’s "unsorted" (ἀκριτόμυθε, 2.246), and `i` gives the sense, never reaching a decision |
| ἀλίαστος (πόλεμος ἀλίαστος, 2.797) | "relentless" | "relentless" | "unceasing" (kept for ἄλληκτον, 2.452), "unyielding", "unrelenting" (the note gives ἀ- + λιάζομαι as a possible origin) |
| εἰσήλυθον (μάχας εἰσήλυθον ἀνδρῶν, 2.798) | "I have gone into" | "I have gone into" | "I have entered", "I have been in"; the aorist of εἰσέρχομαι with a perfect sense |
| φύλλοισιν ἐοικότες ἢ ψαμάθοισιν (2.800) | "like leaves or sands" | "like leaves or sands" | "as numerous as" (the point of the comparison is their number, but the Greek does not say it), "grains of sand"; ψάμαθος is "sand" as in the shipped "sands" (iliad-005, odyssey-009, odyssey-017) |
| προτὶ ἄστυ (2.801) | "toward the town" | "toward the town" | "to the city" (πόλις is "city"); ἄστυ keeps the Odyssey’s "town" |
| ἐπιτέλλομαι (2.802, middle, with a person and an infinitive) | "I enjoin" | "I give this charge" | "I command", "I bid" (reserved for κελεύω); follows ἐπιτέλλω "enjoin / charge" (2.10) and ἐπιτέλλεο "lay these charges" (1.295) |
| πολυσπερέες (πολυσπερέων ἀνθρώπων, 2.804) | "widely scattered" | "widely scattered" | "far-sown", "of many seeds", "scattered far and wide"; πολύς + σπείρω |
| ἄλλη δ’ ἄλλων γλῶσσα (2.804) | "different of different men is the tongue" | "there is a different tongue for each" | "speech" for γλῶσσα in `l` (the Odyssey’s `i` in odyssey-093 has "a different speech for each people"); γλῶσσα keeps "tongue" in `l` |
| σημαινέτω (2.805) | "let him give orders" | "let him give orders" | "signal", "give the word", "mark out"; follows iliad-003’s σήμαιν’ "give orders" |
| ἐξηγείσθω … κοσμησάμενος πολιήτας (2.806) | "let him lead out, having marshalled the citizens" | "lead them out once he has marshalled his fellow-citizens" | "set in array", "draw up"; κοσμέω keeps "marshal" (2.554), and πολιήτης is "citizen" |
| ἔλυσ’ ἀγορήν (2.808) | "loosed the assembly" | "broke up the assembly" | "dissolved" (as a term), "dismissed", "released"; λύω is "loose / release", and `i` takes the sense of ending a meeting |
| τεύχεα (ἐπὶ τεύχεα, 2.808) | "armour" | "armour" | "arms", "gear", "weapons"; follows the Odyssey’s τεύχεα "armour" (12.228, 22.114) |
| ὠΐγνυντο πύλαι (2.809) | "were being opened" | "were opened" | "were thrown open", "flew open" (each adds force); ὀΐγνυμι is "open" |
| πεζοί θ’ ἱππῆές τε (2.810) | "both on foot and horsemen" | "both on foot and mounted" | "infantry and cavalry", "foot-soldiers and charioteers"; the Odyssey’s wording (odyssey-115) |
| ὀρυμαγδός · ὀρώρει (2.810) | "a great din had sprung up" | "a great din went up" | "tumult", "uproar", "had arisen"; follows the Odyssey’s πολὺς … ὀρώρει "a great din" (odyssey-036) and its "had sprung up" |
| κολώνη (αἰπεῖα κολώνη, 2.811) | "hill" | "hill" | "mound" (kept for τύμβος in the Odyssey’s 3.239), "knoll", "barrow"; with αἰπεῖα "steep" |
| περίδρομος (2.812) | "that can be run round" | "with room to run round it" | "encircled", "open on all sides", "with a path round it"; ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα is "on this side and on that" |
| σῆμα (ἀθάνατοι δέ τε σῆμα … Μυρίνης, 2.814) | "tomb" | "tomb" | "sign" (kept for the Odyssey’s σῆμα ἄνακτι, 20.111), "monument", "mound"; a mark over a grave |
| πολυσκάρθμοιο (Μυρίνης, 2.814) | "much-leaping" | "much-leaping" | "swift-leaping", "bounding", "nimble"; πολύς + σκαρθμός "leap", and who Myrine was is not said |
| διέκριθεν (2.815) | "were parted" | "were parted" | "were sorted" (kept for κρίνω), "were divided", "were drawn up" (each decides the sense); the same verb as διακρινέει "parts" (2.387) |
| κορυθαίολος (Ἕκτωρ, 2.816) | "of the glancing helmet" | "of the glancing helmet" (+ note: κόρυς "helmet" + αἰόλος "quick-moving, glancing") | "flashing" (reserved for ἀστεροπητής), "shining" (φαεινός), "gleaming" (γλαυκῶπις), "shifting" (ποικιλομήτης), "tossing-plumed", "with the nodding helm" |
| Πριαμίδης (2.817) | "Priam’s-son" | "son of Priam" | "Priam’s son" unhyphenated in `l`; follows Ἀτρεΐδης "Atreus’-son" / "son of Atreus" |

| Παιήων (5.401) | "Paieon" | "Paieon" | "Paeon" (the familiar English form, turned down so as to keep the spelling of the Odyssey table’s Παιήονος γενέθλης "of the race of Paieon", 4.232), "the physician", "Paian", "Paean" (the god is not the hymn) |
| ὀδυνήφατα φάρμακα (5.401) | "pain-slaying drugs" | "pain-killing drugs" | "soothing drugs", "healing herbs", "pain-relieving"; ὀδύνη "pain" + a root meaning "kill" (usual explanation, not certain); φάρμακον "drug" |
| καταθνητός (5.402) | "subject to death" | "liable to death" | "mortal" (kept for βροτός), "doomed to die", "dying"; κατά + θνῄσκω |
| σχέτλιος ὀβριμοεργός (5.403) | "cruel one, mighty-working" | "a cruel one, a doer of mighty deeds" | "reckless", "violent", "overbearing" (each decides the reproach); ὄβριμος keeps "mighty", σχέτλιος "cruel one" |
| οὐκ ὄθετ’ αἴσυλα ῥέζων (5.403) | "did not heed, doing wicked things" | "did not care that he did wicked things" | "had no scruple", "shrank not from"; ὄθομαι "heed", ῥέζω "do" |
| ἀνῆκε (σοὶ δ’ ἐπὶ τοῦτον ἀνῆκε, 5.405) | "has urged on" | "has urged on" | "set on", "sent against", "incited"; follows the table’s ἀνίημι "urge on" |
| νήπιος (5.406, of Diomedes) | "foolish one" | "foolish as he is" | "fool", "childish"; follows the table’s νήπιος "foolish" (2.38) |
| δηναιός (5.407) | "long-lived" | "long-lived" | "long-lasting", "old"; δηρός "long" family |
| παππάζουσιν (5.408) | "call … ‘papa’" | "call … ‘papa’" | "prattle to", "welcome with a child’s cry"; παππάζω is built on πάππα, a child’s word for father, and the quoted word is kept |
| τὼ νῦν … φραζέσθω μή (5.410) | "So now let … be careful lest" | "So now let … take care lest" | "therefore", "beware", "let him see to it"; τώ = τῷ "so, therefore", φράζομαι "take heed" |
| περίφρων Ἀδρηστίνη (Αἰγιάλεια, 5.412) | "circumspect daughter of Adrastus" | "the circumspect daughter of Adrastus" | "wise", "prudent" (reserved for πεπνυμένος); follows the table’s περίφρων "circumspect"; Ἀδρηστίνη is a feminine patronymic |
| ἰφθίμη ἄλοχος (5.415) | "mighty wife" | "the mighty wife" | "stately wife", "strong"; ἴφθιμος keeps "mighty" |
| ἐϋπέπλων (Ἀχαιϊάδων ἐϋπέπλων, 5.424) | "fair-robed" | "fair-robed" | "well-robed" (the first draft; changed at review, because the Odyssey table fixes Ἀχαιϊάδες εὔπεπλοι, 21.160, as "fair-robed"), "fine-robed", "long-robed" (τανύπεπλος), "beautifully dressed"; πέπλος "robe"; the stock epithet of women, translated every time |
| ὣς φάτο, μείδησεν δὲ πατὴρ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε, / καί ῥα καλεσσάμενος προσέφη χρυσῆν Ἀφροδίτην (5.426–427, two-line speech introduction, female speaker) | "So she spoke, and smiled the father of men and of gods, / and, calling her to himself, addressed golden Aphrodite:" | "So she spoke, and the father of men and of gods smiled, and, calling golden Aphrodite to him, said to her:" | "Thus she spoke", "summoning her", "answered"; follows the table’s ὣς φάτο, μείδησεν δὲ … pattern, ὣς φάτο for a female speaker, πατὴρ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε and the Odyssey’s χρυσέη Ἀφροδίτη "golden Aphrodite"; καλεσσάμενος is "calling … to himself" |
| ἱμερόεντα ἔργα γάμοιο (5.429) | "the works of marriage, full of longing" | "the works of marriage, full of longing" | "lovely works of marriage" (ἱμερόεις keeps "full of longing", as in the table’s ἱμερόεις rows), "desirable"; ἔργα "works" as in πολεμήϊα ἔργα "works of war" |
| δαίμονι ἶσος (5.438, 5.459) | "equal to a divinity" | "like a divinity" | "equal to a god" (reserved for θεός), "like a power" (the Odyssey table’s δαίμων "power" is for one unnamed god acting on a man; a departure, with the reason: here a man is likened to a divine being, and the Iliad has "divinities" for δαίμονας at 1.222), "like a spirit"; the same words at both places |
| δεινὰ δ’ ὁμοκλήσας (5.439) | "dreadfully having shouted at him" | "shouted dreadfully at him" | "threatening", "rebuking" (decide the tone), "with a dread cry"; ὁμοκλάω keeps the Odyssey’s "shouted at" (odyssey-066), and δεινά is the neuter plural as an adverb, "dreadfully" |
| ἀδύτῳ · ἀδύτοιο (5.448, 5.512) | "inner sanctuary" | "inner sanctuary" | "shrine" (the building is the νηός "temple", 5.446), "holy of holies", "adyton"; the word is ἀ- + δύω "enter", the part of a temple not to be entered |
| κύδαινον (5.448) | "were making glorious" | "made him glorious" | "honoured" (kept for τίω), "gave glory to", "restored"; from κῦδος "glory" |
| ἀργυρότοξος (alone, of Apollo unnamed, 5.517) | "the silver-bowed one" | "the silver-bowed one" | "silver-bowed Apollo" (supplies the name the Greek withholds), "the god of the silver bow"; the note names Apollo |
| ἀραιήν (χεῖρα ἀραιήν, 5.425) | "slender" | "slender" | "delicate", "soft", "narrow" (the Odyssey’s "narrow" is of an entrance, ἀραιὴ εἴσοδος), "thin"; ἀραιός is "thin, slight" |
| καρρέζουσα (5.424) | "stroking" | "stroking" | "caressing", "fondling", "petting"; shortened from καταρρέζω, the verb of κατέρεξεν "stroked" (1.361) |
| οὖλος Ἄρης (5.461) | "ruinous Ares" | "ruinous Ares" | "baneful", "destructive", "cursed"; οὖλος keeps the "ruinous" of οὐλομένην (1.2) and οὖλον ὄνειρον (2.6); θοῦρος Ἄρης stays "impetuous Ares" |
| εἰδόμενος (εἰδόμενος Ἀκάμαντι, 5.462) | "making himself like" | "making himself like" | "taking the form of", "in the likeness of", "resembling"; the present participle of εἴδομαι, kept with the table’s ἐεισάμενος "making himself like" |
| ἄκρῃ (Περγάμῳ ἄκρῃ, 5.460) | "high" | "high" | "topmost", "upper", "the summit of"; ἄκρος "high, topmost", and Pergamus is "sacred" at 446, "high" here, as the same citadel |
| ἐς τί ἔτι (5.465) | "to what point still" | "how long" | "to what end", "for what purpose"; ἐς τί "to what (point)", with ἔτι "still" |
| εὖ ποιητῇσι (πύλῃς, 5.466) | "well-made" | "well-built" | "well-wrought", "strongly made"; ποιητός "made", with the table’s ποιητοῖσιν "well-made" / "well-built" (5.198) |
| ἀτὰρ … φέροιεν … ἄγοιεν (5.483–484) | "carry off … bring away" | "carry off … bring away" | "drive away" (the first draft; changed at review, because "drive" is kept for ἐλαύνω and στυφελίζω), "lead" (kept for ἄρχω and ἡγέομαι), "bear off", "take away"; φέρω "carry off" (as the Odyssey, 10.124) and ἄγω of spoil "bring" (1.367, 4.239), the pair for plunder (things carried, animals or people brought) |
| γαμβροῖσι (5.474) | "brothers-in-law" | "brothers-in-law" | "sons-in-law" (the Odyssey’s rendering, where the man is a daughter’s husband), "kinsmen by marriage"; γαμβρός covers any man related by marriage, and Hector’s are his sisters’ husbands |
| ὤρεσσι (5.486) | "wives" | "wives" | "spouses", "mates"; ὄαρ "wife", the usual explanation of a rare word |
| ἕλωρ καὶ κύρμα (5.488) | "prey and spoil" | "prey and spoil" | "prey and booty" (the first draft; changed at review), "plunder"; the pair is the Odyssey’s ἕλωρ καὶ κύρμα γενέσθαι (3.271), shipped in odyssey-011 as "the prey and spoil of birds", and that English is followed; the Odyssey table’s later rows give each word alone "prey" (13.208, 15.480), which cannot serve both halves of a pair |
| πάναγρος (λίνου πανάγρου, 5.487) | "all-catching" | "all-catching" | "all-enclosing", "that takes everything"; πᾶν + ἄγρα "catch" |
| ἁλόντε (dual, 5.487) | "the two of you … having been caught" | "the two of you … caught" | "you both", "the pair of you"; the dual is kept as "the two" |
| ἀλωάς (ἱερὰς κατ’ ἀλωάς, 5.499) | "threshing-floors" | "threshing-floors" | "orchards" (the Iliad’s and Odyssey’s ἀλωή elsewhere, 5.90, 6.293; here the winnowing makes it a threshing-floor), "gardens"; the note says the word has both senses |
| ἀχυρμιαί (5.502) | "chaff-heaps" | "heaps of chaff" | "straw-heaps", "chaff-stacks"; ἄχνη "chaff" (5.499) |
| ὑπολευκαίνονται (5.502) | "grow white beneath" | "grow white beneath" | "whiten", "turn grey"; ὑπο- "beneath, slightly" |
| ἀολλέες (5.498) | "in a close mass" | "in a close mass" | "all together" (reserved for ἅμα / ἀθρόοι), "in a body", "massed"; ἀολλής "crowded together" |
| λαισήϊα πτερόεντα (5.453) | "light shields, winged" | "winged light shields" | "wicker shields", "leather shields", "fluttering shields" (each picks a sense the Greek does not give); λαισήϊον is a kind of shield, the exact kind not known, and πτερόεις "winged" is kept |
| ἐλελίχθησαν (5.497) | "were whirled round" | "wheeled round" | "turned about", "were made to quiver"; passive of ἐλελίζω "whirl, make quiver" (1.530) |
| μεθίστατο (ἑτάροισι, 5.514) | "took his stand among" | "took his place among" | "went over to", "shifted"; μετά + ἵσταμαι "stand among" |
| χρυσαόρου (Φοίβου Ἀπόλλωνος χρυσαόρου, 5.509) | "of the golden sword" | "of the golden sword" | "golden-sworded", "of the golden blade", "with the golden sword" |
| πίονος (ἀδύτοιο, 5.512) | "very rich" (μάλα πίονος) | "very rich" | "fat" (the Odyssey’s πίων is "fat" of flocks and goats), "opulent", "prosperous"; follows the Odyssey table’s πίονα νηόν "a rich temple" (12.346), "rich" of a temple; the Greek does not say rich in what |
| ὦ φίλοι ἀνέρες ἔστε καὶ ἄλκιμον ἦτορ ἕλεσθε (5.529, whole-line exhortation) | "Friends, be men, and take a valiant heart" | "Friends, be men, and take a valiant heart" | "be warriors", "be brave", "summon your courage" (each replaces ἀνέρες or ἦτορ); ὦ φίλοι "friends" as in the shipped rows, ἄλκιμος of persons "valiant", ἦτορ "heart" |
| ἀλλήλους τ’ αἰδεῖσθε κατὰ κρατερὰς ὑσμίνας (5.530) | "and respect one another through the strong battles" | "and respect one another throughout the strong battles" | "feel shame before" (the other sense of αἰδέομαι), "in fierce combat"; keeps the table’s αἰδέομαι "respect" (4.402) and κρατερὴ ὑσμίνη "strong battle" |
| αἰδομένων ἀνδρῶν πλέονες σόοι ἠὲ πέφανται (5.531) | "Of men who feel respect more are safe than have been slain" | "Of men who feel respect, more are safe than are slain" | "survive", "are saved", "than die"; σόος "safe" as in the Odyssey, πέφανται "have been slain" (the root of φένω, not φαίνω) |
| φευγόντων δ’ οὔτ’ ἂρ κλέος ὄρνυται οὔτε τις ἀλκή (5.532) | "but of men who flee neither glory arises, nor any might" | "but when men flee, no glory rises up for them, nor any might" | "defence", "courage" (ἀλκή is "might", as in the table’s θούριδος ἀλκῆς); ὄρνυμαι "arise" |
| ἰωκάς (5.521; rare, sense not certain) | "onsets" | "onsets" (+ note: sense not certain) | "war-cries" (reserved for βοή), "battle-din" (kept for φύλοπις), "rout", "pursuit" (each picks one guess) |
| ἀκροπόλοισιν ὄρεσσιν (5.523; ἀκροπόλος rare, formation not certain) | "high mountains" | "high mountains" | "high-peaked" (the Odyssey’s glossary gloss, but its English at 19.205 is "high mountains"), "lofty" (reserved for ἀγέρωχος), "towering", "topmost"; reused from the Odyssey (odyssey-094) |
| νηνεμίης … ἀτρέμας (5.523–524) | "in windlessness … motionless" | "when no wind blows … motionless" | "in a calm" (reserved for γαλήνη), "in still air", "quietly" |
| μένος Βορέαο (5.524, periphrasis) | "the might of the North Wind" | "the might of the North Wind" | "the force of Boreas", "the North Wind’s fury"; the periphrasis is kept, as with βίη Ἡρακληείη; μένος "might" (2.387), Βορέης "the North Wind" (Odyssey) |
| ζαχρειῶν ἀνέμων (5.525; second part of ζαχρειής not known) | "very violent winds" | "very violent winds" (+ note: the traditional sense) | "furious", "boisterous" (turned down in the Odyssey table for δυσαής), "mighty" (reserved for ἴφθιμος); ζα- "very" as in ζάκοτον |
| πνοιῇσιν λιγυρῇσι (5.526) | "with clear breaths" | "with their clear-sounding breath" | "shrill" (turned down for λιγύφθογγοι), "blasts" (reserved for ἄελλα); λιγυρός "clear" as in the Odyssey’s λιγυρῇ ἀοιδῇ "clear song", πνοιή "breath" as in the table |
| μένω (5.522, 5.571, 5.572, without object) · (5.527, with object) | "stand fast" · "await" | "stood firm" / "hold his ground" / "standing firm" · "awaited" | "stay", "wait" (kept for the table’s ἦ μένετε "Or are you waiting", where the object is a coming event), "withstand"; the intransitive verb is the army’s stand against the Trojans and the transitive one a waiting for the Trojans |
| ὣς Δαναοὶ Τρῶας μένον ἔμπεδον οὐδὲ φέβοντο (5.527) | "So the Danaans awaited the Trojans firmly, nor took flight" | "So the Danaans awaited the Trojans steadily, and did not take flight" | "stood against", "fled" (reserved for φεύγω); ἔμπεδον adverb "firmly" / "steadily" as in the Odyssey (13.86), φέβομαι "take flight" |
| πολλὰ κελεύων (5.528) | "bidding much" | "giving many orders" | "urging", "exhorting" (kept for ὀτρύνω "urge on"); κελεύω "bid, order" |
| πρόμον ἄνδρα (5.533) | "a foremost man" | "a foremost fighter" | "champion" (turned down for πρόμαχος), "man of the front rank", "leader" (reserved for ἀρχός); follows πρόμαχοι "front-fighters" / "foremost fighters" (4.495) |
| ἣ δ’ οὐκ ἔγχος ἔρυτο, διὰ πρὸ δὲ εἴσατο χαλκός (5.538) | "and it did not guard against the spear, but right through rushed the bronze" | "but the shield did not keep the spear out: the bronze sped right through it" | "stop the spear", "turn aside", "pierced" (reserved for πέρησεν); ἐρύομαι "guard" (cf. εἰρύσατο "guarded", 4.185), εἴσατο "rushed / sped", διαπρό "right through" |
| νειαίρῃ ἐν γαστρί (5.539, 5.616; νείαιρα "lowest") | "in the lower belly" | "in the lower belly" | "in the lowest belly", "in the pit of the belly", "in the groin"; νείαιρα "lowest, nether", the part of the belly below the belt |
| ἕλεν … ἄνδρας ἀρίστους υἷε Διοκλῆος (5.541–542) | "took of the Danaans the best men, the two sons of Diocles" | "killed two of the Danaans’ best men, the sons of Diocles" | "slew", "the finest of the Danaans" without the two; ἕλεν "took" in `l` and "killed" in `i` as at 5.144 |
| ἀφνειὸς βιότοιο (5.544) | "rich in livelihood" | "rich in livelihood" | "wealthy in goods", "rich in substance", "rich in cattle"; βίοτος "livelihood" (Odyssey 15.456), ἀφνειός "rich" (2.825) |
| ὅς τ’ εὐρὺ ῥέει Πυλίων διὰ γαίης (5.545) | "who broadly flows through the land of the Pylians" | "which flows broadly through the land of the Pylians" | "wide-flowing", "flowing far" (εὐρύ is an adverb); the river is a god (ὃς τέκετ’ Ὀρτίλοχον), so `l` has "who" |
| διδυμάονε παῖδε (5.548) | "twin sons" | "twin sons" | "two sons" alone, "twin boys", "two children"; διδυμάων "twin" |
| ἡβήσαντε (5.550) | "having come to manhood" | "when they had come to manhood" | "grown up", "come of age", "reached their prime" |
| Ἴλιον εἰς εὔπωλον (5.551) | "to Ilium of the fine foals" | "to Ilium of the fine foals" | "fine-colted" (the table’s ταχύπωλος is "swift-colted", for the people), "well-horsed", "of the fine horses"; reused from the Odyssey (odyssey-005, -052, -066: "Ilios of the fine foals"), with the Iliad’s name for the city |
| τὼ δ’ αὖθι τέλος θανάτοιο κάλυψεν (5.553) | "and the two of them, there, the end of death covered" | "but there the end that death brings covered the two of them" | "death’s end", "the finish of death", "fate" (reserved for μοῖρα); τέλος θανάτοιο follows the table’s ὁπποτέρῳ θανάτοιο τέλος "the end of death … the end that death brings" (3.309); κάλυψεν "covered" as in τὸν δὲ σκότος ὄσσε κάλυψε |
| ἐλάτῃσιν ἐοικότες ὑψηλῇσι (5.560) | "like to high firs" | "like high firs" | "tall firs" (kept for μακρὸν Ὄλυμπον), "lofty" (kept for ἀγέρωχος); ἐλάτη "fir" (odyssey-024), ὑψηλός "high" (3.383) |
| σείων ἐγχείην (5.563) | "shaking his spear" | "shaking his spear" | "brandishing" (kept for ἀμπεπαλών), "waving", "wielding" (kept for νωμάω) |
| τοῦ δ’ ὄτρυνεν μένος Ἄρης (5.563) | "and his might Ares urged on" | "and Ares urged on his might" | "roused his fury" (the table’s μένος of anger is "fury"), "stirred", "spurred"; ὀτρύνω "urge on", μένος "might" |

| ἀντίον ἀλλήλων ἐχέτην (5.569) | "against one another held" | "held out … against one another" | "face to face" (reserved for ἀντίον in a speech formula), "opposite each other" |
| θοός περ ἐὼν πολεμιστής (5.571) | "swift though being a warrior" | "swift warrior though he was" | "swift fighter", "a warrior of speed"; θοός "swift" (2.758), πολεμιστής "warrior" (5.289) |
| δειλώ (dual, of the two dead, 5.574) | "miserable ones" | "miserable men" | "wretched" (reserved for δύστηνος), "poor", "cowardly"; follows δειλός "miserable" (Odyssey 5.299) |
| τυχών · τυχήσας (5.582, 5.579; τυγχάνω of a target, with the part struck) | "having hit" | "hitting him" | "striking", "reaching", "catching"; follows the table’s ἔτυχες "hit" (5.287); βάλλω of a weapon stays "hit" too, the two verbs being told apart by their objects |
| τύχε … ἀμάθοιο βαθείης (5.587; τυγχάνω with the genitive, of a place) | "chanced upon deep sand" | "come down in deep sand" | "hit" (kept for a target), "landed on"; τυγχάνω "chance upon" with the genitive |
| κατὰ κληῗδα (5.579) | "at the collar-bone" | "at the collar-bone" | "at the collarbone" as one word, "on the shoulder", "in the neck" |
| ὑπέστρεφε μώνυχας ἵππους (5.581) | "was turning about the solid-hoofed horses" | "was turning the solid-hoofed horses about" | "wheeling", "driving round"; the table’s μώνυχας ἵππους "solid-hoofed horses" |
| ἡνία λεύκ’ ἐλέφαντι (5.583) | "the reins, white with ivory" | "the reins, white with ivory" | "ivory-white reins", "reins of ivory", "ivory-studded"; the dative is of means and the Greek does not say how the ivory was worked in |
| εὐεργέος δίφρου (5.585) | "the well-made chariot" | "the well-made chariot" | "well-built" (reserved for ἐϋκτίμενος), "well-wrought", "fine"; follows the Odyssey’s ἐυεργέα νῆα "well-made ship" |
| κύμβαχος ἐν κονίῃσιν ἐπὶ βρεχμόν τε καὶ ὤμους (5.586; κύμβαχος and βρεχμός rare) | "head-down in the dust upon the crown of the head and the shoulders" | "head first into the dust, on the crown of his head and his shoulders" (+ note: rare words) | "headlong" (reserved for πρηνής), "on his head", "somersaulting"; "forehead", "skull" (for βρεχμός) |
| ὄφρ’ ἵππω πλήξαντε χαμαὶ βάλον (5.588) | "until the two horses, having struck him, threw him to the ground" | "until the two horses struck him and threw him to the ground" | "kicked" (the Greek does not say how), "knocked"; βάλλω of what is not a weapon is "threw", with the object supplied for both verbs |
| κεκλήγων (5.591) | "shrieking" | "with a shrill cry" | "shouting" (kept for ἄϋσε), "crying out" (kept for ἰάχων), "yelling", "clamouring"; follows iliad-009’s ὀξέα κεκλήγων "shrilly shrieking" |

| ἀοίδιμοι (6.358; rare, "sung of") | "sung-of" | "a subject of song" | "famous in song", "celebrated", "a theme for singers"; ἀοιδή "song" in both; no earlier unit has the word |

| ἐπέσσυται … ἐπαμύνω (6.361) | "is rushing on … come to the defence of" | "is already rushing on … come to the defence of" | "is set", "is eager" (kept for μεμαώς), "defend", "help" (kept for ἀρήγω); follows ἐπάμυνον "come to my defence" (5.685) |
| ποθὴν ἔχουσιν (6.362) | "feel the lack of me" | "feel the lack of me" | "miss me" (kept for ποθέω, 2.703), "long for me", "have longing for"; follows ποθή "the lack of Achilles" (1.240) |
| ὄρνυθι τοῦτον (6.363) | "rouse this man" | "rouse him" | "stir", "urge"; ὄρνυμι "rouse" (the table) |

| οἰκῆας (6.366) | "household servants" | "household servants" | "kinsmen", "slaves", "people of the house"; follows the Odyssey table's οἰκῆες (17.533); kept apart from δμῶες / δμῳαί |

| ἐφεστήκει (6.373) | "was standing on" | "was standing on" | "had taken her stand", "stood"; the pluperfect of ἐφίστημι in the sense of the state, as in the Odyssey's "stand by" |

| ἀγροτέρῳ συῒ καπρίῳ (11.293) | "a wild swine, a boar" | "a wild boar" | "a field boar", "a wild pig and boar" (two nouns collapsed in `i`, both kept in `l`), "a savage boar" |

| μέγα φρονέων (11.296; again μέγα φρονέοντε, 11.325) | "greatly thinking" | "full of proud thoughts" | "exulting", "puffed up", "high-minded", "confident" (each picks a feeling); μέγα "greatly" + φρονέω "think", as in the table’s φίλα φρονέων "thinking kindly" |
| ὑπεραέϊ ἀέλλῃ (11.297) | "a blast blowing from above" | "a storm blowing down from above" (+ note: sense of ὑπερ- not certain) | "a gale from on high", "a howling blast", "a storm-blast"; ἄελλα is "blast" in `l` and "storm" in `i` (table), and ὑπεραής is ὑπέρ "over" + ἄημι "blow" |
| ἀργεστᾶο Νότοιο (11.306) | "of the bright South Wind" | "of the bright South Wind" (+ note: meaning not known) | "clear-skied", "white-clearing", "cloud-clearing", "Argestes" (each picks a sense or makes it a name) |
| τρόφι κῦμα (11.307; τρόφι, old word of uncertain sense) | "swollen" (πολλὸν τρόφι "greatly swollen") | "greatly swollen" (+ note: sense uncertain) | "thickly", "in a mass", "in a heap", "curling" |
| πολυπλάγκτοιο ἰωῆς (11.308) | "of the much-straying … blast" | "of the far-roaming wind … rush" | follows the table’s πολύπλαγκτος (17.425) "much-straying" / "far-roaming"; ἰωή "blast, rush" is new |
| ὣς ἄρα πυκνὰ καρήαθ’ ὑφ’ Ἕκτορι δάμνατο λαῶν (11.309) | "so then thick the heads under Hector were overcome, of the people" | "So thick and fast the heads of the people were overcome beneath Hector" | "fell", "were cut down", "were laid low" (each says how); δάμνημι "overcome" per the table’s δαμνάω "overcame" |
| κέκλετ’ Ὀδυσσεύς (11.312) | "called Odysseus" | "if Odysseus had not called on Diomedes" | "gave orders to" (the table’s `i` for κέκλετο): a departure, because Odysseus is not in command of Diomedes and the verb here is an appeal between equals; `l` keeps "called out to" |
| τί παθόντε λελάσμεθα θούριδος ἀλκῆς; (11.313) | "what having suffered, we two, have we forgotten impetuous might?" | "what has come over the two of us, that we have forgotten impetuous might?" | "what is wrong with us", "why have we forgotten", "have we lost our courage"; the dual participle is kept as "the two of us" |
| ἦδος (μίνυνθα ἡμέων ἔσσεται ἦδος, 11.317–318) | "for a short time of us there will be enjoyment" | "the pleasure of having us will be short" (+ note: exact sense uncertain) | "profit", "use", "joy of us"; ἦδος "pleasure" |
| ἀπέπαυσαν πολέμου (11.323) | "from war they had made them cease" | "had put an end to their fighting" | "killed" (the Greek is the euphemism), "disarmed", "stopped them from war"; ἀποπαύω "make cease" |
| κυδοίμεον (11.324) | "were making uproar" | "went … making an uproar of battle" | "were wreaking havoc", "were making confusion", "were raging"; κυδοιμός "din of battle" |
| ἀσπασίως φεύγοντες ἀνέπνεον Ἕκτορα δῖον (11.326–327) | "gladly fleeing, breathed again from heavenly Hector" | "fleeing from heavenly Hector, drew breath again with joy" | "fleeing gladly", "glad of the respite from", "were glad to flee"; ἀσπασίως "gladly" / "with joy" per the table, ἀναπνέω "draw breath again", δῖος "heavenly" |
| Μέροπος Περκωσίου (11.329) | "Merops the Percosian" | "Merops of Percote" | "Merops of Percote" in `l` (turns the adjective into a place before the note does), "Percosian Merops"; Περκώσιος is the adjective of Περκώτη (2.835), as for Alalcomenean Athena and Hypoplacian Thebe |
| ἀνέρε δήμου ἀρίστω (11.328) | "two men, best of the people" | "two men, the best of the people" | "best of the land" (δῆμος is "land" for a place, "people" for persons: δημογέροντες "elders of the people"), "noblest"; the dual is shown by "two" |
| ἑλέτην δίφρον τε καὶ ἀνέρε (11.328) | "the two took a chariot and two men" | "the two took a chariot and killed two men" | "killed a chariot and two men"; ἑλέτην keeps "the two took" in `l` and "the two killed" in `i` (7.8, iliad-032) and takes "took" for the chariot, "killed" for the men |
| θυμοῦ καὶ ψυχῆς κεκαδών (11.334) | "having deprived of heart and of life" | "deprived of heart and life" | "of life and soul" (the Iliad’s θυμός "life", ψυχή "soul"), "of heart and soul" (a modern idiom of devotion); reused from the Odyssey (odyssey-103, 21.153–154), where θυμός is "heart" and ψυχή "life" |
| ἔνθά σφιν κατὰ ἶσα μάχην ἐτάνυσσε Κρονίων (11.336) | "There for them evenly the fighting stretched the son of Cronus" | "the son of Cronus stretched the fighting out evenly between them" | "made the battle equal", "held the balance of battle", "drew the battle tight" (each explains the rope); τανύω "stretch", κατὰ ἶσα "evenly"; the image is a rope drawn out equally, and the wording is the one to keep if the line recurs |
| ἤτοι ὃ μέν … ὃ δέ (ἤτοι + a subject, 11.338, 11.373) | "For his part, …" · "He then, for his part, …" | "For his part, …" · "He, for his part, …" | "Truly", "Indeed" (the table’s ἤτοι ἐγών "For my part, I" is the pattern), "He then" (the Odyssey’s ἤτοι ὅ γ’, for a man just spoken of); ἤτοι is one word in the edition and opens a contrast with ὃ δέ |
| Παιονίδης (11.339, 11.368) | "Paion’s-son" | "son of Paion" | "the Paeonian" (an adjective of a people, not the patronymic), "Paeon’s son" (to be kept apart from Παιήων "Paieon"); the pattern of Ἀτρεΐδης "Atreus’-son" / "son of Atreus" |
| οὐ δέ οἱ ἵπποι ἐγγὺς ἔσαν προφυγεῖν (11.339–340) | "not for him were the horses near, to flee away on" | "his horses were not near enough for him to escape on" | "within reach", "close enough to flee" (each decides the sense of the infinitive); προφεύγω "flee away" |
| ὀξὺ νόησε κατὰ στίχας, ὦρτο δ’ ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς κεκλήγων (11.343–344) | "sharply noticed through the ranks, and rushed upon them shrieking" | "was quick to notice them along the ranks and rushed upon them with a shrill cry" | "caught sight of" (kept for ἐνόησε at 5.590), "charged" (reserved for ἐπαΐσσω), "calling"; the table’s ὀξὺ νόησε "sharply noticed" / "been quick to notice" and the shipped 5.590 wording for the second half |
| ἀπέλεθρον ἀνέδραμε (ὦκ’ ἀπέλεθρον ἀνέδραμε, 11.354) | "quickly ran back an immeasurable way" | "ran quickly back a very great distance" | "measureless" (turned down at 5.245 and 7.269), "boundless", "a huge way"; ἀπέλεθρος "immeasurable" as in the table’s ἶνα ἀπέλεθρον (5.245, 7.269), here the neuter used of distance; ἀνατρέχω "run back" |
| ἐρωὴν δούρατος (μετὰ δούρατος ᾤχετ’ ἐρωήν, 11.357) | "went after the rush of the spear" | "went after the flight of his spear" | "force" (the table’s i for ἐρωή, said of men), "the cast of the spear", "the course of the spear"; ἐρωή "rush" in `l` as in the table, but `i` takes "flight" when the rush is a missile’s |
| καταείσατο (ὅθι οἱ καταείσατο γαίης, 11.358) | "to where for him it had sped down into the earth" | "to where it had come down in the ground" (+ note: taken as the aorist middle of ἵεμαι with κατά) | "to where it had gone down", "had pierced" (each decides the sense); rare form, the note says how it is taken |
| πληθύς (11.360, 11.405) | "the crowd" | "the crowd" | "the multitude" (iliad-010, -012), "the mass of men" (iliad-066), "throng" (kept for ὅμιλος); πληθύς is "crowd" here, as at 8.142 (iliad-008) |
| κύον (vocative, 11.362) | "dog" | "you dog" | "dog-face" (reserved for κυνῶπα, 1.159), "cur", "hound"; the table’s κύον "dog" (8.423) |
| ᾧ μέλλεις εὔχεσθαι (11.364) | "to whom you are sure to pray" | "to whom you must pray" | "intend to", "are about to" (the table’s μέλλω + infinitive "is sure to be"); εὔχομαι "pray" with a god in the dative |
| ἐξανύω (11.365) | "I shall finish you off" | "I shall finish you off" | "I shall accomplish" (loses the person), "I shall kill you" (decides the object), "run you down"; present with future force, the usual sense "make an end of" |
| ἐπιείσομαι (11.367) | "I shall go against" | "I shall go after" | "I shall attack", "I shall pursue"; ἐπίειμι "go against, go after" |
| στήλη (στήλῃ κεκλιμένος, 11.371) | "pillar" | "pillar" | "gravestone", "stele", "slab"; follows the Odyssey (odyssey-057, "a pillar") |
| ἀνδροκμήτῳ (11.371) | "wrought by men’s toil" | "raised by men" | "man-made", "man-wrought" (drops κάμνω "toil"), "built by human hands"; ἀνήρ + κάμνω |
| βριαρός (κόρυθα βριαρήν, 11.375) | "weighty" | "heavy" | "stout" (reserved for στιβαρός), "mighty" (ἴφθιμος, ὄβριμος), "strong" (κρατερός), "sturdy" (ἄλκιμος); βρίθω "be heavy" |
| πῆχυς τόξου (τόξου πῆχυν ἄνελκε, 11.375) | "the arm of the bow" | "the bow" | "the cubit of the bow", "the bow’s forearm"; what πῆχυς names is not agreed, and `i` leaves it in the bow |
| ταρσὸν δεξιτεροῖο ποδός (11.377; again 11.388 ταρσὸν ποδὸς) | "the flat of the right foot" · "the flat of the foot" | "the flat of his right foot" · "the flat of my foot" | "the sole", "the instep" (each decides the unknown), "the tarsus"; ταρσός is "flat surface" and its place on the foot is not known |
| ἐκ λόχου ἀμπήδησε (11.379) | "out of the ambush leapt up" | "leapt out of his ambush" | "from his hiding-place", "sprang out"; λόχος "ambush" (the table), ἀναπηδάω "leap up" |
| εὐχόμενος ἔπος ηὔδα (of a vaunt, 11.379) | "declaring, spoke a word" | "said, declaring aloud" | "boasting", "vaunting" (kept for ἐπεύχομαι), "praying" (a god is not addressed); εὔχομαι "declare", as at 5.106 |
| ὡς ὄφελον … ἑλέσθαι (11.380–381) | "Would that I had … taken the life out" | "If only I had … taken your life from you" | "I wish I had killed you"; the table’s ὡς ὄφελον "Would that" / "If only", with τοι "from you" |
| πεφρίκασι (οἵ τέ σε πεφρίκασι, 11.383) | "bristle at you" | "bristle with fear at you" | "shudder" (kept for ῥιγέω), "tremble" (τρομέω), "cower" (πτώσσω), "fear" (δείδω); φρίσσω keeps the "bristling" of πεφρικυῖαι (4.282, 7.62) |
| κακότητος (ἀνέπνευσαν κακότητος, 11.382) | "misfortune" | "misfortune" | "baseness" (the Iliad’s κακότης of men in war, 2.368, 3.366), "evil", "wickedness"; here the word is what the Trojans suffer, as in the table’s κακότητα βαρεῖαν "heavy misfortune" (10.71) |
| τοξότα λωβητὴρ κέρᾳ ἀγλαὲ παρθενοπῖπα (11.385) | "Archer, outrager, splendid in your horn, gazer at girls" | "You archer, you outrager, so splendid in your horn, you gazer at girls" | "proud of your bow", "proud of your locks" (each decides the disputed κέρας), "girl-peeper", "ogler"; λώβη "outrage" (1.232), κέρας "horn", ἀγλαός "splendid", ὀπιπεύω "look at" (the note says the formation of παρθενοπῖπα is not certain) |
| κωφὸν … βέλος (11.390) | "blunt … shaft" | "blunt" | "deaf", "feeble" (kept for ἀλαπαδνός), "dull"; the Greek word is "deaf, dull", and of a missile "blunt" |
| ἦ τ’ ἄλλως ὑπ’ ἐμεῖο (11.391) | "Truly otherwise, by me" | "But a shaft from me" | "otherwise it is with me", "far otherwise"; ἦ τε "truly", ἄλλως "otherwise" |
| ἐπαύρῃ (καὶ εἴ κ’ ὀλίγον περ ἐπαύρῃ, 11.391) | "even if it should touch only a little" | "even if it only touches a little" | "grazes" (reserved for ἐπιγράφω), "gets a share of" (the table’s "have the benefit of", 1.410, said of benefit); ἐπαυρίσκω "touch, get a share of", here "touch" |
| ἀκήριον … τίθησι (11.392) | "makes a man spiritless" | "makes a man lifeless" | "heartless" (now means cruel), "uninjured" (the Odyssey’s ἀκήριος, a different word), "dead"; ἀ- + κῆρ "heart", the table’s ἀκήριοι "spiritless" (7.100) with `i` taking the sense of the effect |
| ἀμφίδρυφοί … παρειαί (11.393) | "the cheeks are torn on both sides" | "her cheeks are torn in mourning" | "scratched", "torn all round"; follows ἀμφιδρυφής "torn on both sides" / "with her cheeks torn in mourning" (2.700) |
| αἵματι γαῖαν ἐρεύθων (11.394) | "with blood reddening the earth" | "reddening the earth with his blood" | "staining", "making the earth red", "dyeing"; ἐρεύθω "redden" |
| οἰωνοὶ δὲ περὶ πλέες ἠὲ γυναῖκες (11.395) | "birds are around him, more than women" | "it is the birds, more than the women, that gather round him" | "birds, rather than wives, are about him" (adds a noun), "the vultures"; περὶ πλέες "around, more" |
| οἰώθη (11.401) | "was left alone" | "was left alone" | "was deserted", "was abandoned" (reserved for λείπω), "stood alone"; from οἶος "alone" |
| φόβος ἔλλαβε πάντας (11.402) | "terror seized all" | "terror had seized them all" | "panic" (reserved for φύζα), "fear" (δέος), "flight" (the table’s φόβος in battle, 5.252 and 5.272: a departure from it here, because "flight seized all" is not English and the action is a seizing, as in the table’s φόβον Ἄρηος "terror of battle", 2.767); the table’s Φόβος "Terror" in lower case |
| ἀλλὰ τί ἤ μοι ταῦτα φίλος διελέξατο θυμός; (11.407) | "But why indeed has my dear heart talked these things over with me?" | "But why has my own heart talked all this over with me?" | "debated" (reserved for μερμηρίζω in the table), "argued", "reasoned"; διαλέγομαι "talk through" |
| ῥίγιον (11.405) | "more dreadful" | "more dreadful still" | "colder" (a guess at the derivation), "worse"; follows ῥίγιστα "most dreadful" (5.873) |
| ἐφόβησε (11.406) | "has put to flight" | "has put to flight" | "scared", "frightened" (kept for ταρβέω), "routed"; φοβέω "put to flight" |
| κακοὶ μὲν ἀποίχονται πολέμοιο (11.408) | "the base go away from war" | "the base withdraw from the war" | "cowards" (names the sense), "the worthless" (οὐτιδανοί); κακός of men in battle is "base" (2.365) |
| ἑστάμεναι κρατερῶς (11.410) | "to stand strongly" | "stand his ground strongly" | "stand fast" (kept for μένω), "bravely", "firmly" (ἔμπεδον); κρατερῶς "strongly" |
| ἔλσαν δ’ ἐν μέσσοισι, μετὰ σφίσι πῆμα τιθέντες (11.413) | "and they hemmed him in, in the midst of them, setting woe among themselves" | "and they hemmed him in among them, bringing woe on themselves" | "making trouble for themselves", "preparing their own ruin"; εἴλω keeps "hem in" (1.409), πῆμα "woe" |
| σεύωνται (11.415) | "rush" | "rush" | "set on" (kept for σεύω transitive, iliad-066), "chase", "run"; σεύομαι "rush" |
| ξύλοχος (βαθείης ἐκ ξυλόχοιο, 11.415) | "the deep lair" | "the deep lair" | "thicket" (iliad-028, a lion in a copse), "wood", "covert"; follows the Odyssey’s boar-scene ξύλοχος "lair" (odyssey-096) |
| γναμπτῇσι γένυσσιν (11.416) | "bent jaws" | "curved jaws" | "crooked", "pliant" (the Odyssey’s γναμπτοῖσι μέλεσσι), "hooked"; γναμπτός "bent", the Odyssey’s "bent hooks" |
| κόμπος ὀδόντων (11.417) | "a din of teeth" | "a din of teeth" | "clatter" (kept for ἄραβος ὀδόντων), "gnashing", "clash"; follows the Odyssey’s κόμπος "din" (odyssey-036) |
| οἳ δὲ μένουσιν ἄφαρ δεινόν περ ἐόντα (11.418) | "they await him at once, dread though he is" | "they await him at once, dread though he is" | "stand firm against", "stand their ground" (reserved for μένω intransitive), "straightaway"; μένω transitive "await" (5.527), ἄφαρ "at once" (1.348, 1.594) |
| ἐπάλμενος ὀξέϊ δουρί (11.421) | "springing upon him with a sharp spear" | "springing upon him with a sharp spear" | "leaping at", "bounding up"; ἐπάλλομαι "leap upon", as in iliad-043 and odyssey-068 |
| πρότμησις (κατὰ πρότμησιν, 11.424) | "the lower belly" | "the lower belly" (+ note: usual explanation, not certain) | "the groin", "the navel", "the flank" (each decides the unknown), "the nether belly" (νείαιρα is another word); rare noun, said by the usual explanation to be where the navel-string was cut |
| ἀγοστός (ἕλε γαῖαν ἀγοστῷ, 11.425) | "in the crook of his arm" | "in the crook of his arm" (+ note: sense not known) | "with his palm", "with his hand", "with his elbow" (each decides the unknown); rare noun, usually "the bent arm" or "the hollow of the hand" |
| αὐτοκασίγνητον εὐηφενέος Σώκοιο (11.427) | "own brother of wealthy Socus" | "own brother of wealthy Socus" | "rich" (kept for ἀφνειός), "well-off", "well-endowed"; εὐηφενής is εὖ + ἄφενος "wealth", an epithet of Socus found only here; αὐτοκασίγνητος "own brother" (3.238) |
| ἐπαλεξήσων (11.428) | "to defend him" | "to defend him" | "to ward off for him", "to help him"; the future participle of purpose of ἐπαλέξω, with the dative of the man defended |
| ὦ Ὀδυσεῦ πολύαινε δόλων ἆτ’ ἠδὲ πόνοιο (11.430) | "O Odysseus, much-praised, insatiate of tricks and of toil" | "Odysseus, much-praised, never able to get enough of tricks and toil" | "of much renown", "famous" (κλυτός), "weary of guile"; πολύαινος "much-praised" (9.673, 10.544), ἆτος "insatiate" / "who never has enough of" (the table’s Ἄρης ἆτος πολέμοιο, 5.388, and the Odyssey’s ἆτα δόλων) |
| ἐπεύξεαι (11.431) | "you will vaunt" | "you will cry out in triumph" | "you will boast" (εὔχομαι is "declare"), "you will pray" (the prayer-sense); ἐπεύχομαι keeps "vaunts" / "cries out in triumph" (5.119) |
| τοιώδ’ ἄνδρε κατακτείνας καὶ τεύχε’ ἀπούρας (11.432) | "two such men having killed and their armour having taken away" | "having killed two such men and taken their armour" | "stripped", "despoiled" (ἐναρίζω), "carried off"; ἀπαυράω "take away" (iliad-005, ἑλὼν … ἀπούρας "having taken it away"); the dual τοιώδ’ ἄνδρε is "two such men" |
| οὔτησε κατ’ ἀσπίδα (11.434; οὐτάω of a thrust that lands on the shield and wounds no one) | "thrust at him, upon the shield" | "stabbed at him on his shield" | "wounded" (the table’s οὐτάω; here nothing is wounded, so it would be false), "struck", "pierced"; a departure from the table’s `l` "wounded", with that reason |
| ἔργαθεν (11.437, ἀπὸ … ἔργαθεν χρόα) | "it kept off" | "it kept off" | "tore", "grazed" (each picks a subject and a picture the Greek does not give); ἔργω "shut out, keep off", the subject left as a bare "it" |
| δῖος Νέστωρ (11.510) | "Nestor, heavenly" | "heavenly Nestor" | "noble", "divine" (reserved for θεῖος); the table’s δῖος "heavenly", extended from Odysseus to Nestor |
| ὠμησταί (of birds, 11.454) | "raw-feeding" | "that feed on raw flesh" | "flesh-eating" and "raw-eating" (the table’s ὠμοφάγος "raw-eating" / "that eat raw flesh" is a different word; ὠμηστής keeps ὠμός "raw" with "feeding") |
| ἐρύουσι (11.454, of birds at a corpse) | "will drag at" | "will drag at" | "will tear", "will devour" (go beyond ἐρύω "drag, draw") |
| κτεριοῦσι (11.455) | "will render funeral rites to" | "will pay me funeral honours" | "will bury" (loses κτέρεα, the funeral offerings), "will honour"; follows odyssey-011 (κτερίσειεν), "render him funeral rites" / "pay him funeral honours" |
| κεκλόμενοι (11.460) | "calling out" | "called out" | "urging one another on" (the usual sense of κέλομαι, but the Greek has no "one another"), "shouting" |
| ἐξοπίσω ἀνεχάζετο (11.461) | "to the rear was drawing back" | "kept drawing back toward the rear" | "retreating", "withdrawing"; ἀναχάζομαι keeps the Odyssey table’s "draw back" (Odyssey 11.95) |
| ὅσον κεφαλὴ χάδε φωτός (11.462) | "as much as a man’s head held" | "as loud as a man’s head can hold" | "as loud as he could" (drops the image), "with all his lung"; χανδάνω "hold, contain" |
| ἕπω with ἀμφί (ἀμφὶ δ’ ἄρ’ αὐτὸν Τρῶες ἕπονθ’ 11.474; ἀμφ’ Ὀδυσῆα … Τρῶες ἕπον 11.483) | "kept close" | "kept close" | "followed" (kept for ἕπομαι), "swarmed", "thronged" (too strong a picture); ἕπω "be busy about" |
| θῶες (11.474, 11.479, 11.481) | "jackals" | "jackals" | "wolves", "lions" (λῖς is the lion at 480); the usual identification of θώς |
| ὠμοφάγοι θῶες (11.479) | "raw-eating jackals" | "jackals that eat raw flesh" | follows the table’s ὠμοφάγοισιν "raw-eating" / "that eat raw flesh" |
| κεραὸν ἔλαφον (11.475) | "horned deer" | "horned deer" | "stag" (reserved for ὑψίκερων ἔλαφον), "antlered"; follows the table’s ἔλαφος "deer" |

| ἐϋπλόκαμος Ἑκαμήδη (11.624) | "fine-plaited Hecamede" | "fine-plaited Hecamede" | "fair-haired", "fair-tressed" (reserved for ἐυπλοκαμῖδες), "fine-haired"; the table’s ἐϋπλόκαμος "fine-plaited" |

| ἐπιπροΐηλε τράπεζαν (11.628) | "set out a table" | "set out a table" | "pushed up", "brought"; a rare compound taken as "set out before", and the note says so |

| οὔατα (of a cup, 11.633) | "ears" | "handles" | "ears" in `i` (not English for a cup), "grips", "lugs"; the Greek word is "ears", and the note says it is the handles |
| δοιαὶ δὲ πελειάδες ἀμφὶς ἕκαστον χρύσειαι νεμέθοντο (11.634–635) | "two doves around each one, golden, were feeding" | "round each of them two golden doves were feeding" | "pecking", "grazing", "perched"; νεμέθομαι "feed", πέλεια "dove" (5.778), the count (two on each, or one on each side) left as in the Greek |

| ὁρόω (11.651) | "I see" | "I see" | "I perceive", "I recognise" (kept for γιγνώσκω); the uncontracted ὁρόω |

| οἷος ἐκεῖνος δεινὸς ἀνήρ (11.653–654) | "what kind that one is, a dread man" | "what a man he is, a dread man" | "terrible", "fearsome" (αἰνός), "formidable"; δεινός keeps "dread" (1.200) |
| τάχα κεν καὶ ἀναίτιον αἰτιόῳτο (11.654) | "quickly he might even blame one blameless" | "he might very soon blame even the blameless" | "perhaps", "readily" for τάχα; follows odyssey-099 (ἀναίτιον αἰτιόῳο) "blameless" / "blame" |

| ἤλιθα πολλήν (11.677) | "exceeding much" | "a very great" | "an abundance of", "plentiful", "untold"; ἤλιθα "exceedingly" |

| ἐλίγαινον (11.685) | "cried out clearly" | "cried out clearly" | "proclaimed in shrill tones", "shrilled" (the table’s λιγύς is "clear"); λιγαίνω "cry in a clear voice" |

| ἄμμι (11.714) | "to us" | "to us" | epic dative of ἡμεῖς |
| ἀέκοντα … ἐσσυμένους (11.716–717) | "not unwilling … very eager" | "not unwilling but very eager" | "reluctant", "hasty"; ἀέκων "unwilling" (the table’s ἀέκοντος), ἐσσυμένος "eager" |

| βοῦν ἀγελαίην (11.729) | "a cow of the herd" | "a cow from the herd" | the Odyssey table’s row (17.181), unchanged |

| Μούλιος (11.739) | "Mulius" | "Mulius" | "Moulios"; Latinised like the other Greek names |
| χαλκήρεϊ δουρί (11.742) | "bronze-fitted spear" | "bronze-fitted spear" | the table’s row (4.469, 5.309), unchanged |
| ἤριπε δ’ ἐν κονίῃσιν (11.743) | "crashed down in the dust" | "crashed down in the dust" | follows the table’s ἤριπε "crashed down" (4.462) |

| ὀδὰξ ἕλον οὖδας (11.749) | "with their teeth bit the ground" | "bit the earth with their teeth" | the Odyssey table’s row (22.269), unchanged |
| ἀλάπαξα (Μολίονε παῖδ’ ἀλάπαξα, 11.750) | "I would have laid waste" | "I would have laid waste" | "cut down", "slain", "destroyed" (each changes the verb); ἀλαπάζω "lay waste" as in the table, here of persons |

| ἐγγυάλιξε (μέγα κράτος, 11.753) | "put into their hands … great strength" | "put great strength into the hands of" | "gave", "granted victory"; ἐγγυαλίζω "put into the hands", κράτος "strength" as in the table (1.509) |
| σπιδέος πεδίοιο (11.754) | "the broad plain" | "the broad plain" | "wide", "open"; σπιδής "wide, spacious" |
| ἀνὰ … ἔντεα καλὰ λέγοντες (11.755) | "gathering up the fine gear" | "gathering up the fine gear" | "picking up", "collecting the weapons", "armour" (reserved for τεύχεα); ἀναλέγω "gather up", ἔντεα "gear" as in the table’s ἔντεα (3.339) and at 731 (ἐν ἔντεσιν, "in his own gear") |
| βήσαμεν ἵππους (11.756) | "made our horses go" | "brought our horses" | "drove", "halted"; causative aorist of βαίνω |
| Βουπράσιον · Ἀλήσιον · Ὠλενίη · Θρυόεσσα · Ἀρήνη · Μινυήϊος · Ὑπειροχίδης · Ἀγαμήδη (names, 11.711–756) | "Buprasium" · "Alesium" · "Olenian" · "Thryoessa" · "Arene" · "Minyeïus" · "Hypeirochus" · "Agamede" | same | "Bouprasion", "Alesion"; Latinised like the other Greek names, with neuter -ον names given Latin -um as in the table’s Thryum and Dium |
| εὐχετόωντο (11.761) | "prayed" | "offered their prayers" (+ note: the verb also means "vow" or "boast") | "gave thanks", "praised", "boasted"; εὐχετάομαι "pray" with the sense of honour paid noted |
| ὣς ἔον, εἴ ποτ’ ἔον γε (11.762) | "So was I, if ever I was" | "That is what I was, if ever I was" | "such was I", "so I was, if ever"; ἔον first-person imperfect |
| ἀρετῆς ἀπονήσεται (11.763) | "will have the benefit of his excellence" | "will have the benefit of his excellence" | "enjoy his valour", "profit from his prowess"; follows the table’s ἀρετή "excellence" (8.535); ἀπονίνημι "have the benefit of" is new here |

| ἀάατον (Στυγὸς ὕδωρ, 14.271; meaning not known) | "inviolable" | "inviolable" (+ note: meaning not known; "not to be harmed" is the traditional gloss) | "harmless" (the Odyssey’s 21.91 guess, wrong for an oath), "unfailing", "dread" (reserved for δεινός) |
| μαρμαρέη (ἅλα μαρμαρέην, 14.273) | "gleaming" | "gleaming" | "sparkling" (kept for μαρμαίροντα, 20), "shimmering", "glittering" |
| ὑποταρτάριοι (θεοί, 14.279) | "beneath Tartarus" | "beneath Tartarus" | "in Tartarus", "of Tartarus", "underworld" |
| ἄϊστος (14.258) | "unseen" | "never to be seen again" / "vanished from sight" | "unknown", "invisible", "lost" |
| Χάριτες (Χαρίτων μίαν ὁπλοτεράων, 14.267) | "one of the younger Graces" | "one of the younger Graces" | "Charites", "Gracious ones"; ὁπλότερος "younger" |
